#!/bin/bash
#FLUX --queue=bhuwan --gpus=1
#FLUX --job-name=chunk
#FLUX --output="./slurm_logs/{id}.out"

# NOTE: This script appears to take command-line arguments. To run it as a Flux job,
# you would submit it like: flux submit ./script.sh arg1 arg2

RUN_NAME="nofix_crf_512_$1"
MODEL_NAME="crf" # or "longformer"
OUTPUT_DIR="./runs/${RUN_NAME}"

hostname
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=gpu_name,memory.total,memory.free --format=csv

# conda activate base
echo 'env started'

echo 'logging into wandb'
wandb login
export WANDB_PROJECT=thesis
export WANDB_WATCH=all

echo 'invoking script to train chunk'
context_length=512
curr_split=$1
time python3 run_chunk.py \
    --output_folder=${OUTPUT_DIR} \
    --model_name=${MODEL_NAME} \
    --model_num=$2 \
    --train_set="./split_data/processed_data/${curr_split}/train_${context_length}_chunk_CE.pkl" \
    --valid_set="./split_data/processed_data/${curr_split}/dev_${context_length}_chunk_CE.pkl" \
    --learning_rate=1e-5 \
    --random_seed=75 \
    --dropout=0 \
    --max_len=256 \
    --num_epochs=20 \
    --weight_decay=0.01 \
    --batch_size=8 \
    --num_labels=14 \
    --context_length=${context_length} \
    --gold_file="split_data/datasets/${curr_split}/dev-task-flc-tc.labels.txt"
echo 'done'

    # --train_set="./processed_data/train_${context_length}_chunk.pkl" \
    # --valid_set="./processed_data/dev_${context_length}_chunk.pkl" \

issues: The job requests a GPU but does not explicitly request any CPU resources via --ntasks or --cpus-per-task. Flux will likely default to allocating a single CPU core. This can create a significant performance bottleneck, as the CPU may be unable to keep the GPU fed with data, leading to underutilization of the expensive GPU resource. It is recommended to explicitly request a reasonable number of CPUs (e.g., --cpus-per-task=8) to support the GPU workload.
The output file is directed to a subdirectory (`./slurm_logs/`). The script does not create this directory, which will cause the job to fail at launch if the directory does not exist.

The script relies on two command-line arguments (`$1` and `$2`) but includes no checks to see if they are provided. If the job is submitted without them, the variables will be empty, and the script will likely fail with errors related to file paths (`--train_set`) and other parameters (`--model_num`).
